nodes.text: Microarray Normalization Method Comparison (ExpressionNormalizationWorkflow). Bioc Workflow ExpressionNormalizationWorkflow analog: read raw microarray CEL/IDAT files, normalize with multiple methods (RMA, vsn, lumi, ComBat), compare normalization quality via PCA and variance estimation. For normalization quality comparison and method selection ONLY — NOT for differential expression statistical testing. For differential expression analysis from a normalized microarray count matrix, use nf-core/differentialabundance.

For normalization quality comparison and method selection ONLY — NOT for differential expression statistical testing. For differential expression analysis from a normalized microarray count matrix, use nf-core/differentialabundance.

Germline variant calling and rare disease annotation from WES data — identify rare pathogenic variants in protein-coding regions | germline short-variant calling from paired-end whole-exome sequencing FASTQ/BAM (alignment, duplicate marking, base recalibration, HaplotypeCaller) followed by VEP annotation and rare disease filtering (gnomAD allele frequency, ClinVar, deleteriousness scores) → annotated filtered VCF of candidate rare disease variants

RNA-seq expression outlier and aberrant splicing analysis for rare disease — detect genes with abnormal expression or splicing that may explain the phenotype | RNA-seq alignment and quantification from paired-end FASTQ (STAR alignment, gene/transcript counting) followed by expression outlier analysis (OUTRIDER / DROP-style aberrant expression and splicing detection) to identify genes with statistically significant expression deviations → ranked list of expression outlier genes and aberrant splicing events

Integrate WES variant calls with RNA-seq expression outlier results to prioritize candidate causal genes for the rare disease phenotype | integration of germline variant calls (filtered annotated VCF) with RNA-seq expression outlier and aberrant splicing results — cross-reference genes with rare damaging variants against genes showing expression or splicing outliers, rank by combined evidence (variant pathogenicity + expression z-score + splicing deviation) → prioritized candidate gene list with integrated evidence scores

RNA-seq differential expression analysis to identify differentially expressed genes between conditions | differential gene expression on bulk RNA-seq data (alignment, quantification, DESeq2/edgeR negative-binomial model), two-group or multi-group comparison → per-gene log2 fold change and adjusted p-values

ATAC-seq open chromatin profiling to identify accessible regulatory regions | ATAC-seq peak calling and accessibility analysis from paired-end FASTQ (adapter trimming, alignment, duplicate removal, MACS2 narrow peak calling, accessibility quantification) → peak set and per-peak accessibility scores

ChIP-seq transcription factor binding analysis to identify TF binding peaks | ChIP-seq peak calling for transcription factor binding from paired-end FASTQ (alignment, duplicate removal, MACS2 narrow peak calling with input control, peak annotation) → TF binding peak set and per-peak enrichment scores

Integrate RNA-seq differential genes with ATAC-seq accessibility regions and ChIP-seq TF binding peaks, link peaks to genes via genomic proximity / correlation | multi-omics integration of transcriptomic differential results with epigenomic peak sets — peak-to-gene linking by genomic proximity and/or accessibility-expression correlation, overlay of TF binding with accessible regions and DE genes, fluentGenomics-style integrated analysis → linked peak-gene-TF regulatory network and concordance summary

Germline variant calling and annotation on the patient's WES data for rare disease diagnosis | germline short-variant calling from paired-end whole-exome FASTQ (alignment, duplicate marking, base recalibration, HaplotypeCaller, VEP annotation, rare-variant filtering) → annotated VCF of candidate rare variants

RNA-seq processing with aberrant expression and aberrant splicing outlier detection on the patient's RNA-seq data | RNA-seq alignment and quantification with aberrant expression and aberrant splicing outlier detection (DROP-style) → per-gene expression outliers and splicing outliers supporting variant interpretation

Integrate WES rare variants with RNA-seq expression/splicing outliers to prioritise the causal gene/variant for the rare disease workup | integration of annotated rare germline variants with transcriptomic outlier evidence — cross-layer variant prioritisation → ranked candidate causal genes/variants with supporting RNA evidence

Guide assignment for Perturb-seq CRISPR screen: process guide-capture reads from single-cell CRISPR screen data, assign sgRNA guides to individual cells, and construct a cell × guide assignment matrix. Reference: Replogle JM et al. 2022 Cell 185(14):2559-2575 (DOI: 10.1016/j.cell.2022.05.013). | sgRNA guide-to-cell assignment from single-cell CRISPR screen data (guide capture read processing, barcode demultiplexing, cell-guide matrix construction) → cell × guide assignment matrix

Hit calling for Perturb-seq CRISPR screen: identify significant gene perturbations from the single-cell expression data with guide assignments, performing per-guide differential expression analysis, effect size estimation, and FDR-controlled hit calling. Reference: Replogle JM et al. 2022 Cell 185(14):2559-2575. | perturbation hit calling from single-cell CRISPR screen data (per-guide differential expression, effect size estimation, multiple-testing correction, FDR control) → ranked list of significant gene perturbations with effect sizes

Perturbation state embedding using scVI/scANVI: learn a latent embedding of single-cell expression profiles conditioned on guide assignments using scVI (unsupervised) and scANVI (semi-supervised with perturbation labels), characterizing perturbation effects in the latent space. Reference: Replogle JM et al. 2022 Cell 185(14):2559-2575. | perturbation state embedding using variational inference (scVI unsupervised latent model, scANVI semi-supervised with perturbation labels) on single-cell expression profiles with guide annotations → latent embedding and perturbation effect characterization in latent space

Assign CRISPR guide RNAs to single cells in Perturb-seq data following Replogle et al. 2022 | guide RNA assignment and cell barcode demultiplexing from Perturb-seq single-cell sequencing data → cell-to-guide mapping and annotated single-cell expression matrix

Hit calling and differential perturbation effect testing against non-targeting controls | statistical hit calling and differential expression testing comparing perturbation groups to non-targeting controls → hit table and perturbation effect sizes

Perturbation state representation and embedding using scVI and scANVI | deep generative modeling of perturbation transcriptional states using scVI and semi-supervised scANVI → low-dimensional latent space embedding and perturbation clustering

RNA-seq + Epigenomic Integration (fluentGenomics). Bioc Workflow `fluentGenomics` analog: integrate RNA-seq differential genes with ATAC-seq accessibility regions and ChIP-seq TF binding peaks, link peaks to genes via + .

Perturb-seq guide assignment: assign gRNAs to individual cells from the CRISPR screen single-cell sequencing data (Replogle et al. 2022 Cell design) | guide RNA assignment in a single-cell CRISPR screen (Perturb-seq) — count gRNA UMIs per cell barcode from guide library sequencing, apply assignment thresholds → cell-by-guide assignment matrix linked to gene expression barcodes

Perturb-seq hit calling: identify significant perturbation hits from the guide-assigned single-cell data | perturbation hit calling on guide-assigned Perturb-seq data — per-perturbation differential expression against non-targeting controls, multiple-testing correction → ranked list of significant gene perturbation hits

Perturbation state analysis: learn scVI/scANVI latent embedding of perturbed cells to characterize perturbation-induced transcriptional states | deep generative modeling of perturbed single-cell expression profiles with scVI/scANVI — integrate cells across perturbations into a latent space, annotate perturbation states → latent embedding, perturbation clusters, and state annotations

Identify tumor-reactive T cells from scRNA-seq data, including T cell subset annotation, TCR clonotype reconstruction, and tumor-reactivity marker characterization | T cell subset identification and tumor-reactive T cell characterization from single-cell RNA-seq data — clustering, cell-type annotation, TCR V(D)J reconstruction and clonotype expansion analysis, tumor-reactivity marker scoring → tumor-reactive T cell clusters, clonotype tables, and marker gene lists

Predict neoantigens from tumor somatic mutations — call somatic variants from tumor WES/WGS, predict mutant peptide HLA binding affinity, and rank candidate neoantigens | neoantigen prediction pipeline from tumor sequencing data — somatic variant calling (tumor vs normal), HLA typing, mutant peptide binding affinity prediction (NetMHCpan/NetMHC), variant annotation and peptide generation → ranked candidate neoantigen list with binding affinity scores

Integrate tumor-reactive TCR clonotypes from scRNA-seq with predicted neoantigens to identify TCR–neoantigen pairs and characterize tumor-reactive T cell responses | integration of TCR clonotype data from scRNA-seq with neoantigen prediction results — TCR specificity matching, neoantigen-reactive clonotype identification, and cross-referencing T cell receptor sequences with predicted mutant peptide-HLA complexes → matched TCR–neoantigen pairs and tumor-reactive clonotype annotations

Identify tumor-reactive T cells from scRNA-seq data | identification of tumor-reactive and tumor-infiltrating T cell states and clonotypes from scRNA-seq expression data using activation, exhaustion, and cytotoxicity signatures → annotated T cell subsets and reactivity scores

Predict candidate neoantigens and peptide-MHC binding affinities | neoantigen prediction and peptide-MHC binding affinity prediction from tumor somatic variants and HLA alleles → ranked list of candidate immunogenic neoepitopes

Find tumor-reactive T cells in this scRNA-seq data | identification of tumor-reactive T cells from single-cell RNA-seq (with paired TCR/VDJ data) — cell clustering, T cell subset annotation, TCR clonal expansion analysis, exhaustion/cytotoxicity signature scoring → ranked tumor-reactive T cell clusters and clonotypes

Predict neoantigens from tumor variants | neoantigen prediction from tumor somatic variants (WES/WGS VCF) with HLA typing — mutant peptide generation and MHC class I binding-affinity prediction (pVACseq/netMHCpan-style) → ranked candidate neoantigen peptides

IDAT → Normalisation → Differential Methylation → Gene Enrichment. EPIC/450K array methylation from IDAT — minfi load + functional normalisation, DSS differential methylation, missMethyl gene-set enrichment. Use when you want the DSS-based differential-methylation + enrichment wrapper chain. Also applicable to bismark bisulfite coverage from nf-core/methylseq.

Load EPIC/450K IDAT files and perform functional normalisation with minfi | methylation array IDAT loading and functional normalisation (minfi preprocessNoob/functional normalisation) on Illumina EPIC or 450K BeadArray IDAT files → normalised beta/M value matrix

Perform differential methylation analysis using DSS on the normalised methylation matrix | differential methylation analysis (DSS DML/DMR testing) on a normalised beta/M value matrix from Illumina methylation arrays, two-or-more-group comparison → per-CpG and DMR statistics with FDR

Run missMethyl gene-set enrichment analysis on the differentially methylated CpGs | gene-set enrichment analysis (missMethyl gometh/gsameth) on differentially methylated CpG lists from Illumina array data, accounting for probe bias → enriched GO/KEGG pathways
Run RNA-seq analysis and differential expression

Graph-based pseudotime trajectory inference with Monocle3 (R) on the user's single-cell AnnData h5ad, using monocle_cluster and root_cell parameters to order cells along the learned principal graph | graph-based pseudotime trajectory inference on a processed single-cell AnnData (h5ad) using Monocle3 — cluster cells, learn principal graph on the UMAP embedding, order cells from a user-specified root cell → per-cell pseudotime values (csv), trajectory/UMAP plots (png), annotated h5ad output

RNA velocity estimation with scVelo (Python) on the same single-cell AnnData h5ad, using the user-specified velocity_mode (e.g., dynamical/stochastic) to compute spliced/unspliced velocity dynamics | RNA velocity estimation on a single-cell AnnData (h5ad) with spliced/unspliced count layers using scVelo — preprocess, compute moments, recover dynamics in the specified velocity_mode → per-cell velocity and velocity graph, velocity stream/embedding plots (png), annotated h5ad output

Load EPIC/450K IDAT methylation array files and perform functional normalisation with minfi | Illumina EPIC/450K methylation array preprocessing from raw IDAT files (minfi read.metharray + functional normalisation, probe filtering) → normalised beta/M-value matrix

Run DSS differential methylation analysis on the normalised methylation matrix | differential methylation analysis on a normalised methylation matrix (DSS beta-binomial model), two-group comparison → differentially methylated loci (DML) and regions (DMR) with statistics

Run missMethyl gene-set enrichment on the differentially methylated loci | gene-set enrichment on differentially methylated CpG loci (missMethyl gometh, bias-corrected for probe multiplicity) → enriched GO/KEGG gene sets

Predict CYP450 inhibition (major isoforms: CYP3A4, CYP2D6, CYP1A2, CYP2C9, CYP2C19) for a new chemical entity — requires SMILES input | CYP450 enzyme inhibition prediction from a molecular structure (SMILES/SDF) — classification of inhibition liability across major CYP isoforms (CYP3A4, CYP2D6, CYP1A2, CYP2C9, CYP2C19) → per-isoform inhibition probability or IC50 category

Predict hepatic clearance for a new chemical entity — requires SMILES input and/or in vitro intrinsic clearance (CLint) values | Hepatic clearance prediction from a molecular structure (SMILES) and/or in vitro intrinsic clearance — well-stirred or parallel-tube liver model scaling using CLint, fu, Qh → predicted hepatic clearance (CLh) and extraction ratio

Run RNA-seq analysis: QC, adapter trimming, alignment, and per-gene quantification on user's RNA-seq data | bulk RNA-seq processing from FASTQ files — quality control, adapter trimming, alignment to reference genome, and per-gene quantification → gene count matrix and aligned BAM files

Run differential expression analysis on the gene count matrix from step 1 | differential gene expression on a bulk RNA-seq gene count matrix (DESeq2/edgeR negative-binomial model), two-group or multi-group comparison → per-gene log2 fold change and adjusted p-values

Illumina 450k/EPIC Methylation Array DMR Analysis (methylationArrayAnalysis). Bioc Workflow `methylationArrayAnalysis` analog: read IDAT files via minfi, QC, normalize (SWAN or noob), call DMPs (limma), DMRs (DMRcate), gene-set test (missMethyl).

Illumina 450k/EPIC Methylation Array DMR Analysis (methylationArrayAnalysis). Bioc Workflow `methylationArrayAnalysis` analog: read IDAT files via minfi, QC, normalize (SWAN or noob), call DMPs (limma), DMRs (DMRcate), gene-set test (missMethyl).

Estimate human PK parameters from animal PK data (rat, mouse, dog) using inter-species allometric scaling | allometric inter-species scaling from preclinical animal PK data (clearance, volume of distribution) to estimate human first-in-human PK parameters

Run full mechanistic PBPK compartmental simulation with organ-specific clearances and renal/hepatic impairment submodels | mechanistic physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) simulation with multi-organ compartments and special population impairment models for dose adjustment

Run Monte Carlo sampling across virtual patient populations for PK variability and uncertainty characterization | Monte Carlo population simulation on PBPK models to quantify parameter uncertainty and inter-individual pharmacokinetic variability

Estimate human PK parameters from preclinical animal (rat, mouse, or dog) data via allometric scaling and IVIVE | inter-species allometric scaling of PK parameters (clearance, volume of distribution, half-life) from rat/mouse/dog to human using power-law scaling and/or IVIVE hepatic clearance prediction → predicted human CL, Vd, t½ with R² fit metrics

Full PBPK simulation with compartmental model and organ-specific clearance, including optional renal/hepatic impairment submodel for special population dosing | whole-body PBPK simulation using a multi-compartment physiological model (organ-specific clearance, tissue partitioning, absorption) with optional renal impairment (eGFR-based) or hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh) submodel → plasma concentration-time profiles, AUC, Cmax, Tmax for healthy and special populations

Monte Carlo sampling for variability characterization across the simulated population | Monte Carlo population variability simulation sampling covariate distributions (body weight, age, organ blood flows, enzyme abundance, renal function) across the PBPK model → population PK parameter distributions, 5th/50th/95th percentile concentration-time profiles, variability characterization for regulatory submission

Estimate human PK parameters from preclinical animal data (rat, mouse, or dog) via allometric/inter-species scaling | inter-species allometric scaling of preclinical pharmacokinetic data (clearance, volume of distribution, half-life from rat/mouse/dog) → predicted human PK parameters (CL, Vd, t1/2) for first-in-human dose projection

Run full mechanistic PBPK simulation with compartmental organ model and organ-specific clearance, including optional renal/hepatic impairment submodels for special population dosing | mechanistic whole-body PBPK simulation with compartmental organ model and organ-specific (hepatic/renal) clearance, with optional renal- and hepatic-impairment submodels → plasma and tissue concentration-time profiles for healthy and special populations

Run Monte Carlo sampling on the PBPK model to characterize inter-individual variability | Monte Carlo population variability sampling over PBPK model parameters (physiological and compound-specific) → population PK distributions, prediction intervals, and variability characterization for regulatory packages

Find drugs with transcriptional signatures matching the RNA-seq differential expression results using LINCS/L1000 connectivity map | query LINCS L1000 / CMap perturbation database with a ranked gene signature from differential expression → ranked list of drugs/compounds with similar or opposing transcriptional profiles, mechanism-of-action inference

Run RNA-seq differential expression analysis to derive the transcriptional signature (treatment/disease vs control) | differential gene expression on bulk RNA-seq data, two-group comparison → per-gene log2 fold change and adjusted p-values defining an up/down-regulated gene signature

Find drugs whose perturbation transcriptional signatures match (or reverse) the RNA-seq signature via LINCS L1000 / Connectivity Map-style signature querying | drug repurposing by transcriptional signature matching — query LINCS L1000 / Connectivity Map perturbagen signatures with a differential expression signature → ranked compounds with concordant or reversing connectivity scores

Validate and standardize SMILES input file with identifier pairs | input validation, canonicalization, and quality filtering of SMILES strings with molecule IDs → cleaned SMILES file
RDKit RECAP decomposition into core scaffolds and R-groups | fragmentation of validated SMILES using RDKit RECAP rule-based cleavage → decomposed scaffolds and attached R-groups

Generate matched molecular pairs and compute property deltas using mmpdb | matched molecular pair indexing and property delta computation on fragmented chemical series via mmpdb → MMP index database and fragment transformation delta table

Rank novel scaffolds by frequency, drug-likeness, and synthetic accessibility (SA score) | prioritization and ranking of unique scaffolds based on occurrence frequency, drug-likeness metrics, and synthetic accessibility score (SA score) → ranked scaffold summary table

Phase A — Cardiovascular safety pharmacology simulation (ICH S7A core battery): in silico hERG and cardiac ion-channel inhibition, QT prolongation / proarrhythmia risk, and hemodynamic endpoints (blood pressure, heart rate, ECG) for the user's compound | in silico cardiovascular safety pharmacology panel on a small-molecule SMILES — hERG and cardiac ion-channel inhibition prediction, QT/proarrhythmia risk scoring, hemodynamic endpoint prediction → per-endpoint inhibition values and risk scores

Phase B — CNS safety pharmacology simulation (ICH S7A core battery): CNS off-target receptor panel, blood-brain barrier penetration, and functional observational battery / locomotor activity endpoints for the user's compound | in silico central nervous system safety pharmacology panel on a small-molecule SMILES — CNS off-target receptor profiling, BBB penetration prediction, functional observational battery / behavioral endpoint risk → per-endpoint risk scores

Phase C — Respiratory safety pharmacology simulation (ICH S7A core battery): respiratory rate, tidal volume, and respiratory-relevant off-target endpoints for the user's compound | in silico respiratory safety pharmacology panel on a small-molecule SMILES — respiratory function endpoint risk (rate, tidal volume) and respiratory-relevant off-target profiling → per-endpoint risk scores

Validate SMILES input file (one SMILES+ID per line) for MMP pipeline | SMILES validation and parsing from a text file (one SMILES+ID per line) — RDKit canonicalization, invalid-entry flagging → validated SMILES list with IDs

RDKit RECAP decomposition of validated SMILES into scaffold + R-groups | RECAP (Retrosynthetic Combinatorial Analysis Procedure) decomposition of validated SMILES into scaffold and R-group fragments using RDKit → fragment-scaffold mapping table

Run mmpdb to compute property deltas for fragment swaps from RECAP decomposition | Matched Molecular Pair analysis using mmpdb — compute property/activity deltas for fragment transformations (R-group swaps) from decomposed molecules → MMP rules with delta property values

Rank novel scaffolds by frequency, drug-likeness, and SA score from MMP analysis | Ranking of novel scaffolds identified from MMP analysis by frequency of occurrence, drug-likeness (Lipinski/QED), and synthetic accessibility (SA) score → ranked scaffold table with scores

Validate SMILES input file (one SMILES + compound ID per line) | validate a SMILES input file (one SMILES + ID per line) — RDKit parsing, sanitization, flag invalid/duplicate entries → cleaned validated SMILES+ID table

RDKit RECAP decomposition of validated molecules into scaffolds + R-groups | RECAP retrosynthetic fragmentation of validated small molecules with RDKit → per-compound scaffold cores and R-group fragment sets

mmpdb matched molecular pair indexing: property deltas for fragment swaps | matched molecular pair analysis with mmpdb — index fragment-swap transforms across the compound set and compute per-transform property deltas → queryable MMP database

Rank novel scaffolds by frequency, drug-likeness, and SA score | rank novel scaffolds emerging from MMP analysis by occurrence frequency, drug-likeness (QED-style), and synthetic accessibility (SA score) → prioritized ranked scaffold list
Validate RNA-seq expression matrix and clinical metadata | validation and quality control of RNA-seq expression matrix and clinical metadata table → validated matrix and aligned sample metadata

Differential expression using voom transformation, linear model with covariates, eBayes, and topTable | differential gene expression analysis on RNA-seq counts using limma-voom linear modeling with clinical covariates and empirical Bayes moderation → logFC, adjusted p-values, and normalized expression matrix

Gene signature scoring via GSVA/ssGSEA on MSigDB hallmark gene sets to identify top enriched pathways per group | single-sample pathway enrichment scoring using GSVA or ssGSEA on 50 MSigDB hallmark gene sets across sample groups → pathway enrichment score matrix and top enriched pathways

Validate expression matrix and clinical metadata for downstream limma-voom and GSVA/ssGSEA analysis | QC and validation of a gene expression matrix (counts or log-transformed) paired with clinical/sample metadata — check sample ID concordance, missing values, library size distribution, and metadata completeness → validated expression matrix and metadata ready for statistical modeling

Voom transformation, linear model with covariates, eBayes, topTable to produce logFC and adj.P.Val per gene | limma-voom differential expression analysis on a validated RNA-seq count matrix with clinical covariates — voom precision-weighted transformation, linear model fitting with covariates, empirical Bayes moderation, topTable extraction → per-gene log2 fold change and adjusted p-values

GSVA/ssGSEA on hallmark MSigDB (50 gene sets) to identify top enriched pathways per group | GSVA/ssGSEA gene set enrichment analysis on an expression matrix using the MSigDB hallmark 50 gene sets collection — compute per-sample enrichment scores, rank pathways by enrichment, identify top enriched pathways per group → ranked pathway enrichment table and per-sample GSVA score matrix

Validate expression matrix + clinical metadata (sample concordance, missing values, covariate integrity) | validation and QC of a pre-computed gene expression matrix with matched clinical/sample metadata — sample concordance checks, missing-value and covariate integrity checks → validated analysis-ready expression matrix and metadata table

limma-voom differential expression with covariates: voom transformation, linear model, eBayes, topTable (logFC, adj.P.Val) | differential gene expression on a pre-computed expression matrix using limma-voom (voom precision weights, linear model with covariate adjustment, empirical Bayes moderation) → per-gene log2 fold change and adjusted p-values (topTable)

GSVA/ssGSEA gene signature scoring on MSigDB hallmark gene sets (50 sets); top enriched pathways per group | gene set enrichment scoring (GSVA/ssGSEA) of a processed expression matrix against the 50 MSigDB hallmark gene sets → per-sample pathway enrichment scores and top enriched pathways per group
